Sa ating Panginoong Diyos, dahil sa lungkot, pangamba, at pagkadismaya na bumabalot sa atin.
At sa aking mga kapatid sa Iglesia Ni Cristo, mga taong lubos kong tinitingala ngunit kailangan kong tawagan ng pansin. Mahal ko kayong lahat, ngunit ito rin ang nagtulak sa akin para ihayag ang matagal ko nang napapansin.
Pinakinggan ko kayo noon. Sana’y mabigyan niyo rin ako ng pagkakataon ngayon.

“Dapat panagutin ang lahat ng mapatutunayang sangkot sa kurapsyon na yan, sinuman sila, anuman ang kanilang posisyon sa gobyerno, dapat silang panagutin.”

Matapos malantad ang matinding katiwalian kaugnay ng flood control projects, sunod-sunod ang mga demonstrasyon na nananawagan sa imbestigasyon at pagpapanagot sa mga maysala. Isa ang INC sa mga nagsulong ng parehong layunin at nanawagan sa administrasyong Marcos na seryosohin ito.
Kaisang-diwa ako dito. Tama lang na ipaglaban ang katotohanan at katarungan.

Tayo ba ay para sa katotohanan at katarungan, o nais lamang ipagtanggol ang kaalyado at tuligsain ang kalaban?

“Kaya natin sila pinili at ibinoto sa ating pag-aakala na sila po ay gagawa ng mabuti sa kapakanan po ng sambayanang Pilipino.
Pero sila po ang sumira sa pagtitiwala nating iyon.“

Una, naniniwala ako na may mga kritisismo sa INC na paninira o pang-uusig lamang. Hindi ako sang-ayon sa mga gawa-gawang paratang, at umaasa ako na mabigyan rin sila ng pagkakataong maunawaan ang ating pananampalataya.

Ngunit, naniniwala ako na maling ituring na pang-uusig kaagad ang lahat ng puna, lalo kung ito ay nakaaapekto na sa buong bansa.
Para ba talaga saan, o kanino, tayo tumitindig?
Mula Pagsamba ng Kabataan hanggang sa katandaan, laging pinapaalala ang kahalagahan ng katapatan at pananagutan. Hinahanap sa bawat kapatid ang mga katangiang nakasulat sa Bibliya, at handa tayong tawagan ng pansin ang mga pagkukulang sa layong maging sakdal at kalugod-lugod ang ating paglilingkod sa Panginoong Diyos.
Masigasig tayo sa loob ng Iglesia, pero ganito rin ba tayo para sa bayan?
Ang pandarambong ni Joseph Estrada, pandar

deduped_items.summary: An INC member pens an open letter to his fellows: 'Ang hindi ko lang maunawaan, bakit ang imbestigasyon kay Pang. Ferdinand Marcos at kanyang mga kaalyado ay nararapat para sa hustisya at katotohanan, pero pagdating kay VP Sara Duterte at Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, ito ay panggigipit at pamumulitika lamang?'
deduped_items.body_text:
“Huwag kayong padaya kaninuman sa pamamagitan ng mga pangangatuwirang walang kabuluhan, sapagkat dahil nga sa mga ito, ang Diyos ay napopoot sa mga suwail. (…)
Sapagkat pawang mabuti, matuwid at totoo ang ginagawa ng namumuhay sa liwanag. Sikapin ninyong matutunan kung ano ang kalugud-lugod sa Panginoon.
Huwag kayong makibahagi sa mga gawain ng kadiliman na walang ibinubungang mabuti. Sa halip ay ibunyag ninyo ang mga iyon.”
Efeso 5:6, 9-11
– Excerpt from a weekend INC worship service, June 6, 2026
Bago ang lahat, nais kong humingi ng paumanhin.
Sa aking mga kaibigan, kakilala, at kapwa Pilipino na nalilito, naguguluhan, at nagagalit sa mga nagaganap.
Sa ating Panginoong Diyos, dahil sa lungkot, pangamba, at pagkadismaya na bumabalot sa atin.
At sa aking mga kapatid sa Iglesia Ni Cristo, mga taong lubos kong tinitingala ngunit kailangan kong tawagan ng pansin. Mahal ko kayong lahat, ngunit ito rin ang nagtulak sa akin para ihayag ang matagal ko nang napapansin.
Pinakinggan ko kayo noon. Sana’y mabigyan niyo rin ako ng pagkakataon ngayon.
Selective justice
“Dapat panagutin ang lahat ng mapatutunayang sangkot sa kurapsyon na yan, sinuman sila, anuman ang kanilang posisyon sa gobyerno, dapat silang panagutin.”
– Bro. Bienvenido Santiago Jr., INC General Evangelist at Rally for Transparency and a Better Democracy, November 16, 2025
Matapos malantad ang matinding katiwalian kaugnay ng flood control projects, sunod-sunod ang mga demonstrasyon na nananawagan sa imbestigasyon at pagpapanagot sa mga maysala. Isa ang INC sa mga nagsulong ng parehong layunin at nanawagan sa administrasyong Marcos na seryosohin ito.
Kaisang-diwa ako dito. Tama lang na ipaglaban ang katotohanan at katarungan.
Ang hindi ko lang maunawaan, bakit ang imbestigasyon kay Pang. Ferdinand Marcos at kanyang mga kaalyado ay nararapat para sa hustisya at katotohanan, pero pagdating kay VP Sara Duterte at Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, ito ay panggigipit at pamumulitika lamang?
Oo, mas malaki ang trilyones na nilimas sa flood control kumpara sa milyon-milyong hindi maipaliwanag na confidential funds o undeclared campaign donations, ngunit hindi ba’t dapat mabigyang-linaw ang parehong isyu? Bakit nagbabago ang pananaw natin, depende sa personalidad na nasasakdal?
Tayo na ang nagsabi: “Selective justice is INJUSTICE”
Muli, tama at makatarungan lang na kalampagin ang gobyerno na panagutin ang mga sangkot sa flood control corruption, ngunit ang panawagang ito ay mawawalan ng kredibilidad at magiging kaduda-duda kung isasantabi na lang ang iba pang isyu ng katiwalian.
Tayo ba ay para sa katotohanan at katarungan, o nais lamang ipagtanggol ang kaalyado at tuligsain ang kalaban?
Accountability
“Kaya natin sila pinili at ibinoto sa ating pag-aakala na sila po ay gagawa ng mabuti sa kapakanan po ng sambayanang Pilipino.
Pero sila po ang sumira sa pagtitiwala nating iyon.“
– Bro. Arnel Tumanan at EDSA Rally, July 1, 2026
Una, naniniwala ako na may mga kritisismo sa INC na paninira o pang-uusig lamang. Hindi ako sang-ayon sa mga gawa-gawang paratang, at umaasa ako na mabigyan rin sila ng pagkakataong maunawaan ang ating pananampalataya.
Ikalawa, hindi rin ako sang-ayon na wala tayong karapatang mag-rally gayong binoto natin sila. Constitutional right ng bawat mamamayang Pilipino na ihayag ang kanilang mga saloobin, at dapat lamang na singilin ang mga opisyal na pinagkatiwalaan natin.
Ngunit, naniniwala ako na maling ituring na pang-uusig kaagad ang lahat ng puna, lalo kung ito ay nakaaapekto na sa buong bansa.
Para ba talaga saan, o kanino, tayo tumitindig?
Mula Pagsamba ng Kabataan hanggang sa katandaan, laging pinapaalala ang kahalagahan ng katapatan at pananagutan. Hinahanap sa bawat kapatid ang mga katangiang nakasulat sa Bibliya, at handa tayong tawagan ng pansin ang mga pagkukulang sa layong maging sakdal at kalugod-lugod ang ating paglilingkod sa Panginoong Diyos.
Masigasig tayo sa loob ng Iglesia, pero ganito rin ba tayo para sa bayan?
Ang pandarambong ni Joseph Estrada, pandar

deduped_items.title: Indonesian authorities arrest former anti-corruption prosecutor after seizing US$19 million and gold
deduped_items.summary: Former anti-graft prosecutor Febrie Adriansyah has been accused of money laundering while serving as Indonesia’s top anti-corruption prosecutor. He denied wrongdoing after being questioned on Friday (Jul 24), saying he was a victim of “criminalisation”.
deduped_items.body_text:
Indonesian authorities arrest former anti-corruption prosecutor after seizing US$19 million and gold
Former anti-graft prosecutor Febrie Adriansyah has been accused of money laundering while serving as Indonesia’s top anti-corruption prosecutor. He denied wrongdoing after being questioned on Friday (Jul 24), saying he was a victim of “criminalisation”.
JAKARTA: Indonesian authorities arrested a former anti-graft prosecutor after seizing millions of dollars and more than 70 kilogrammes of gold bars from his home and other properties, an official said on Friday (Jul 24).
Southeast Asia's biggest economy has long struggled with corruption and has arrested scores of public officials in recent years.
Febrie Adriansyah stands accused of money laundering while serving as the country's top anti-corruption prosecutor, Assistant Attorney General for Oversight Rudi Margono told reporters late on Friday.
Febrie stepped down on Jul 11 after serving in the role for more than four years, following the raids on properties, including his house outside Jakarta.
Investigators seized US$19 million in various currencies and 74 kilogrammes (163 pounds) of gold bars worth millions more.
After hours of questioning, Febrie denied any wrongdoing late Friday and said he was a victim of "criminalisation" in comments to local TV.
His lawyer Febri Diansyah said his client hoped that "the legal process can proceed fairly."
The investigation against Febrie was started by police, then handed over to anti-corruption specialists in his former office.

deduped_items.title: Indonesian authorities arrest former anti-corruption prosecutor after seizing US$19 million and gold
deduped_items.summary: Former anti-graft prosecutor Febrie Adriansyah has been accused of money laundering while serving as Indonesia’s top anti-corruption prosecutor. He denied wrongdoing after being questioned on Friday (Jul 24), saying he was a victim of “criminalisation”.
deduped_items.body_text:
Indonesian authorities arrest former anti-corruption prosecutor after seizing US$19 million and gold
Former anti-graft prosecutor Febrie Adriansyah has been accused of money laundering while serving as Indonesia’s top anti-corruption prosecutor. He denied wrongdoing after being questioned on Friday (Jul 24), saying he was a victim of “criminalisation”.
JAKARTA: Indonesian authorities arrested a former anti-graft prosecutor after seizing millions of dollars and more than 70 kilogrammes of gold bars from his home and other properties, an official said on Friday (Jul 24).
Southeast Asia's biggest economy has long struggled with corruption and has arrested scores of public officials in recent years.
Febrie Adriansyah stands accused of money laundering while serving as the country's top anti-corruption prosecutor, Assistant Attorney General for Oversight Rudi Margono told reporters late on Friday.
Febrie stepped down on Jul 11 after serving in the role for more than four years, following the raids on properties, including his house outside Jakarta.
Investigators seized US$19 million in various currencies and 74 kilogrammes (163 pounds) of gold bars worth millions more.
After hours of questioning, Febrie denied any wrongdoing late Friday and said he was a victim of "criminalisation" in comments to local TV.
His lawyer Febri Diansyah said his client hoped that "the legal process can proceed fairly."
The investigation against Febrie was started by police, then handed over to anti-corruption specialists in his former office.

deduped_items.title: JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings
deduped_items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China’s JD.com has partnered with Iraqi digital commerce platform GINI to increase access to its goods in Iraq, marking the latest step toward developing the country’s rapidly […] The post JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings appeared first on Iraqi News.
deduped_items.body_text:
JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China’s JD.com has partnered with Iraqi digital commerce platform GINI to increase access to its goods in Iraq, marking the latest step toward developing the country’s rapidly expanding e-commerce industry.
The deal would integrate JD.com’s product catalog into GINI’s digital marketplace and the SuperQi app, providing Iraqi customers with greater access to items from one of China’s top online retailers.
The agreement aims to establish a direct supply chain between JD.com and the Iraqi market, thereby enhancing product availability and facilitating cross-border online buying.
GINI, an Iraqi digital commerce and market automation platform, combines merchants, delivery providers, and payment services in a unified ecosystem, allowing companies to manage sales, payments, and logistics.
JD.com, founded in 1998, is China’s largest retailer by revenue and one of the country’s leading e-commerce companies, with a vast logistics network that enables rapid order fulfillment across China and international markets.
The agreement comes as Iraq’s e-commerce sector grows, along with rising internet penetration, digital payment adoption, and government efforts to modernize the economy and encourage more private sector investment in technology and digital services.
Baghdad has increasingly pushed to recruit multinational technology businesses and digital commerce platforms as part of larger attempts to diversify the economy away from oil, generate private-sector employment, and enhance access to products and services via online markets.

deduped_items.title: Youth account bill grants children NT$1.14 million
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Youth account bill grants children NT$1.14 million- By Jonathan Chin / Staff writer, with CNA
 The opposition-controlled legislature yesterday passed legislation to establish state-sponsored savings accounts aimed at boosting the nation’s birthrate by supporting childrearing and granting eligible citizens a total of at least NT$1.14 million (US$35,231) throughout their first 18 years. The bill proposed by the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) and the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) passed a third reading after a long deadlock in a vote down party lines. The law, called the Taiwan Youth Development and Future Account Act (台灣兒少成長及未來帳戶條例), is now headed for the president’s desk. Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) and Taiwan People’s Party legislators hold signs to celebrate the passage of a bill to establish child growth and future accounts at the Legislative Yuan in Taipei yesterday.Photo: Wang Yi-sung, Taipei Times The law would create two accounts for each eligible newborn: a “Taiwan future account,” which is locked until the recipient turns 18, and an “education and development account,” with funds that could be accessed at any time. The government would open the two accounts for Taiwanese nationals who are under 18 years of age after 183 days of residency in a fixed abode on the nation’s soil, the act says. Corporations and relatives may put more money into the future account, but with significant limits on parents’ ability to access the funds. The Taiwan future account, which cannot be accessed until adulthood, could be used for the holder’s education, vocational training, professional needs, creating a start-up or housing, the law says. It would have an initial deposit of NT$60,000 and start receiving NT$30,000 annually when the account holder is six years old and end when they turn 18. The account holder, their legal guardian or close relatives may put money into the account until the account holder is 18, with no limit on the maximum annual sum. A sponsoring corporation could put up to NT$50,000 a month into an account and receive tax breaks or other incentives in exchange. The education and development account would receive an annual subsidy of NT$60,000 for account holders under seven years old, after which they would receive NT$30,000 per year until they turn 18. These accounts can be accessed any time. The Bureau of Labor Insurance will manage funds in the future accounts and guarantee returns no lower than banks’ two-year time-deposit rate, while the national treasury would cover any shortfall. The opposition’s original bill included an article that would have given corporations that sponsor Taiwan future accounts a fixed tax break. The provision was omitted in the final version, after Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) lawmakers argued that it would create a tax haven for super-rich people and exacerbate income inequality. Instead, the incentive would be determined by the government administratively. Social welfare authorities can remove control of the accounts from parents who abandon, abuse or otherwise neglect the rearing and education of their children. The agency-in-charge must return any money that had been appropriated for improper use to the account holder. The program is expected to roll out next year and cost NT$200 billion annually, according to information previously released by the government. In the Cabinet’s version, it had proposed a NT$5,000 monthly growth allowance for children until the age of 18 as part of President William Lai’s (賴清德) 18-point population strategy. The scheme would have transferred the NT$5,000 monthly subsidy to parents until the child was six, after which half would be put into a government-managed account that the child could access at 18. DPP Legislator Fan Yun (范雲) said that social experts have warned that the KMT-TPP proposal allowing additional deposits into future accounts by parents and businesses would worsen inequality through reverse redistribution. deduped_items.title: USTR notices a 10% tariff on Taiwan under Section 301
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            USTR notices a 10% tariff on Taiwan under Section 301COMPETITIVE EDGE: The 10 percent would not be stacked on MFN duties, placing Taiwan in a better position than rivals like China, academics said- Staff writer, with CNA
 The Office of the US Trade Representative’s (USTR) announcement of a 10 percent tariff on certain Taiwanese products — which was to take effect yesterday US time — is not final, but would depend on a separate investigation into alleged structural excess capacity and production in Taiwan’s manufacturing sector, Vice Premier Cheng Li-chiun (鄭麗君) said yesterday. The USTR in March announced that it had launched an investigation into excess capacity and production, as well as another probe into whether 60 economies had taken steps to ban imports of goods produced with forced labor, citing Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The probes were intended to determine whether those US trading partners had engaged in acts, policies or practices that are unreasonable or discriminatory, and have therefore “burdened” or “restricted” US commerce, the USTR said. A US flag flies off the stern of a tour boat at the Port of Los Angeles in California on July last year.Photo: AFP According to a pre-publication version of the USTR Federal Register notice on Thursday, if the most-favored-nation (MFN) tariff on a product from Taiwan is below 10 percent, the combined MFN and Section 301 tariff would total 10 percent. Products already subject to an MFN tariff of 10 percent or more would not face an additional Section 301 duty. After the two investigations have been completed, the final tariff rate would be subject to a final determination by Washington, said Cheng, convener of the Cabinet’s Taiwan-US Economic and Trade Task Force. The USTR’s announcement on Thursday recognized Taiwan’s commitment under the Taiwan-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade to ban imports of goods produced using forced labor, Cheng said. Taiwan and the EU were the only two trading partners among the 60 economies to receive a 10 percent tariff rate that was not added to their existing MFN duties, giving them the most favorable treatment. Taiwan Institute of Economic Research (TIER, 台經院) president Chang Chien-yi (張建一) said that Taiwan’s lower tariff burden could bolster the competitiveness of local traditional manufacturers, giving them an edge over rivals in Japan and China that face higher duties amid US investigations into forced labor concerns. Nonetheless, uncertainty persists over the outcome of a separate US probe into industrial overcapacity, with the findings expected by the end of this month, Chang said. The investigation could have wider implications for Taiwan’s semiconductor industry and warrants close monitoring, he said. TIER economist Liu Pei-chen (劉佩真) said that advanced-node foundries should be less affected, while mature-node foundries could face greater exposure, as concerns about excess capacity are concentrated in that segment. Chang added that Taiwan exports relatively few semiconductors directly to the US, with many shipped elsewhere for assembly into information and communications technology products. The impact could be greater if Washington imposed tariffs on finished products containing chips not manufactured in the US, he said. Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research (中華經濟研究院) president Lien Hsien-ming (連賢明) agreed that Taiwan’s 10 percent tariff rate puts the economy in a relatively favorable position compared with Japan and South Korea, particularly for traditional manufacturing sectors. The overcapacity investigation is more likely to weigh on mature-node semiconductor production, while advanced chipmaking should remain largely unaffected, reflecting Taiwan’s critical role in the global technology supply chain, Lien said. Additional reporting by Crystal Hsu

deduped_items.title: US tariff hikes dismay and anger trading partners
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            US tariff hikes dismay and anger trading partners- AP, BANGKOK
 US President Donald Trump’s latest set of tariff hikes yesterday drew objections the US’ trading partners, including China and Japan, with Australia slamming them as “completely unjustified.” The Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) late on Thursday announced extra tariffs of 10 to 12.5 percent on 60 economies, saying the countries had failed to adequately enforce a ban on goods made with forced labor. The new tariffs took effect just as stopgap levies Trump imposed after a stinging defeat at the Supreme Court expired at 12:01am yesterday. A customer shops for food at a supermarket in London yesterday.Photo: EPA Australian Minister for Trade and Tourism Don Farrell rejected claims linking Australia, a major exporter of beef, gold and copper, to modern slavery and raising the tariff on its exports to the US to 12.5 percent from the 10 percent level imposed after Trump’s “Liberation Day” hikes last year. “We believe that amongst all of the countries in the world Australia does take the issue of slavery, modern slavery, seriously, and will continue to do that,” Farrell told reporters in Adelaide. Australia believes the higher tariffs are “completely unjustified and we will continue to lobby the United States Trade Representative to remove all tariffs on Australian goods,” Farrell said. New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said the tariffs on his country, also subject to a 12.5 percent import duty, were “extremely disappointing,” unjustified and harmful to trade. A US investigation serving as the basis for the tariffs did not provide meaningful evidence to support allegations of forced labor. “Tariffs are not the way — they drive up costs and uncertainty for businesses,” he wrote on X. EU High Representative of Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas questioned the US’ stance in comments on Channel News Asia. “If you compare our labor laws to the ones of the United States, I mean we have, people have paid vacations, we have very good conditions, labor conditions for our employees, so it’s not really grounded,” Kallas said. Also facing a 12.5 percent tariff, Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry, which reiterated its stance of not condoning the use of forced labor, said it would “continue to engage the USTR to explore options.” Japan likewise protested the 12.5 percent tariff imposed on its exports, saying Tokyo had been reassured by the Trump administration that there would be no more tariffs on top of an earlier agreement on a 10 percent US duty. “Our understanding is both sides are still committed to that,” Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told a routine news conference. “It is regrettable that the measure imposes tariffs on the grounds of non-existence of measures banning imports of goods made by forced labor, even though Japan’s industry and trade are in line with international rules,” Kihara said. South Korea said it would maintain close communication with the US to preserve a mutual “balance of benefits.” The South Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resource said the announcement eased some uncertainty over US trade policy, but noted that a Section 301 investigation into alleged South Korean excess production continues. The combined duties on South Korean exports should not exceed 15 percent, the ministry said in a statement. Thailand noted it is subject to the new 12.5 percent tariff by the US under the forced labor provision, but the measure exempts around 2,120 items, representing more than half the value of Thai goods exported to the US. Thailand is also monitoring the possibility of an additional tariff on the grounds of structural overcapacity under another ongoing US probe against 16 countries, but Washington has not yet announced those results, the Thai Ministry of Commerce said in a statement. The Southbound Travel for Guangdong Vehicles scheme was extended to cover five more cities – Shenzhen, Foshan, Dongguan, Huizhou and Zhaoqing – from Saturday, with the daily quota of urban trips doubling to 200. A total of nine mainland cities in the Greater..
deduped_items.body_text:
Nearly 170 mainland Chinese motorists expected in Hong Kong under expanded scheme
Southbound Travel for Guangdong Vehicles scheme extended to five additional cities from Saturday, with daily quota of urban trips doubling to 200
Close to 170 mainland Chinese motorists are expected to arrive in Hong Kong on Saturday under an expanded cross-border travel scheme, with hotels rolling out accommodation, dining, shopping and parking packages to attract the new visitors.
The Southbound Travel for Guangdong Vehicles scheme was extended to cover five more cities – Shenzhen, Foshan, Dongguan, Huizhou and Zhaoqing – from Saturday, with the daily quota of urban trips doubling to 200.
A total of nine mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area are now eligible, comprising the five new additions and the original four of Guangzhou, Zhuhai, Jiangmen and Zhongshan.
Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said authorities received three times as many applications under the expanded scheme as the available quota.
“The response has been very encouraging,” Chan said at the scheme’s launch ceremony at the Hong Kong port of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge.
“Of the applications received, 60 per cent came from the five newly added cities.”

deduped_items.body_text:
Heatwaves come and go, and while this is happening with 
increasing frequency and intensity – as this year’s record-breaking temperatures show – they slip from attention once things cool off. What does not disappear is the lasting and costly damage they do to the basic infrastructure we rely on in our daily lives.
Ultra-hot days and nights can result in the 
deaths of many people (those who cannot afford air conditioning especially) and they ignite 
forest infernos of terrifying intensity. Some of these make the news but what does not usually make headlines is the damage to roads, railways, bridges and other infrastructure.
Yet the cost is there, mounting more rapidly as each sweltering summer arrives – and it will have to be paid for by current and future generations. It is a cost that could eventually run into trillions of dollars.
Human-activity-induced climate change in general, and its manifestation in the form of stifling heat in particular, has been 
overshadowed by renewed wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, but the consequences mount with each fractional rise in summer temperatures and they cannot be ignored.
Some are taking notice. On July 15, Reuters reported on Europe’s race to protect infrastructure from heat as “railways buckle under record heat, roads melt and power grids strain”. A recently published book, Climate Change Effects on Infrastructure, examines how facilities are operating outside or at the limit of tolerance levels because they were built on assumptions that did not include climate change or extreme weather.
The problem is not, of course, confined to the European continent, and it is hardly a new one. As a report by the UN Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) noted back in 2023, “
Infrastructure financing and climate change are the most pressing issues facing Asia and the Pacific today.”

deduped_items.body_text:
Nearly 170 mainland Chinese motorists expected in Hong Kong under expanded scheme
Southbound Travel for Guangdong Vehicles scheme extended to five additional cities from Saturday, with daily quota of urban trips doubling to 200
Close to 170 mainland Chinese motorists are expected to arrive in Hong Kong on Saturday under an expanded cross-border travel scheme, with hotels rolling out accommodation, dining, shopping and parking packages to attract the new visitors.
The Southbound Travel for Guangdong Vehicles scheme was extended to cover five more cities – Shenzhen, Foshan, Dongguan, Huizhou and Zhaoqing – from Saturday, with the daily quota of urban trips doubling to 200.
A total of nine mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area are now eligible, comprising the five new additions and the original four of Guangzhou, Zhuhai, Jiangmen and Zhongshan.
Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said authorities received three times as many applications under the expanded scheme as the available quota.
“The response has been very encouraging,” Chan said at the scheme’s launch ceremony at the Hong Kong port of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge.
“Of the applications received, 60 per cent came from the five newly added cities.”

Close to 170 mainland Chinese motorists are expected to arrive in Hong Kong on Saturday under an expanded cross-border travel scheme, with hotels rolling out accommodation, dining, shopping and parking packages to attract the new visitors.
The Southbound Travel for Guangdong Vehicles scheme was extended to cover five more cities – Shenzhen, Foshan, Dongguan, Huizhou and Zhaoqing – from Saturday, with the daily quota of urban trips doubling to 200.
A total of nine mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area are now eligible, comprising the five new additions and the original four of Guangzhou, Zhuhai, Jiangmen and Zhongshan.
Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said authorities received three times as many applications under the expanded scheme as the available quota.
“The response has been very encouraging,” Chan said at the scheme’s launch ceremony at the Hong Kong port of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge.
“Of the applications received, 60 per cent came from the five newly added cities.”

deduped_items.title: Herbicide banned in 70 countries to be pulled from sale in Australia by chemical maker
deduped_items.summary: Syngenta says it will stop selling paraquat in Australia after new regulations on chemical linked to Parkinson’s diseaseGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastSyngenta, the producer of a herbicide banned in more than 70 countries and which has been linked to Parkinson’s disease, will stop selling paraquat in Australia, saying new regulations has made it “commercially unviable”.The decision to pull the product follows new restrictions on the highly poisonous chemical announced
deduped_items.body_text:
Syngenta, the producer of a herbicide banned in more than 70 countries and which has been linked to Parkinson’s disease, will stop selling paraquat in Australia, saying new regulations has made it “commercially unviable”.
The decision to pull the product follows new restrictions on the highly poisonous chemical announced by the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority in June.
Paraquat has been produced by the Swiss company for decades, but has long been linked to Parkinson’s disease in users.
It is banned in more than 70 countries and has been prohibited in the European Union since 2007.
It cannot be used in domestic settings in Australia, but is still widely used in agriculture, particularly broad-acre cropping like grains, sugarcane and cotton. The APVMA assessed that the weight of evidence does not show that paraquat exposure through approved uses increases the risk of developing Parkinson’s disease.
But it did impose new restrictions to address acute exposure and risks to animals.
The company said the decision to pull the products followed a commercial review carried out in the wake of the APVMA’s rules.
Syngenta ANZ’s managing director, David Van Ryswyk, said the company will manage the phase-out of its paraquat products in strict alignment with the APVMA’s designated sell-out and use-by timelines.
“Regulatory constraints, combined with a highly complex and increasingly expensive supply chain, have made the paraquat herbicide products commercially unviable,” Van Ryswyk said.
The new restrictions on the herbicide required that backpack sprayers be phased out, mandate additional personal protective equipment for users and set a much lower maximum rate of application per hectare.
At the time of the APVMA’s decision, Syngenta said the pesticide “does not cause an unacceptable environmental impact” and that the regulation would limit its use in a significant number of crop use cases.
The company had planned to continue supplying through a third-party manufacturer, but on Friday it said the new regulations and an increasingly expensive supply chain had made the product unviable.
Generic paraquat products will still be available for local farmers.
Last month, the Melbourne neurologist Associate Prof Wes Thevathasan told the ABC that there has been “global consensus” in his field that exposure to paraquat was linked to the development of Parkinson’s disease.
“There are now multiple epidemiological studies or real-world exposure studies that have suggested that paraquat increases the risk of Parkinson’s disease by around threefold,” Thevathasan said.
Grain Producers Australia spokesperson Andrew Weidemann said Syngenta’s decision created uncertainty for local growers.
“Its withdrawal leaves some important questions about what happens next,” he said.
“Australia is a relatively small market, and decisions like this call future investment into question.
“If companies cannot see sufficient value in maintaining products here, growers risk being left with fewer choices at the same time we urgently need more tools to manage herbicide resistance.”

deduped_items.title: Lofty ambitions: can puffer jackets be made more sustainable?
deduped_items.summary: As temperatures dip, the puffer’s appeal inflates. But quality and filler are factors to consider before buying newChange by degrees offers life hacks and sustainable living tips each Saturday to help reduce your household’s carbon footprintGot a question or tip for reducing household emissions? Email us at changebydegrees@theguardian.comWhether you call it a parka, puffer or Tassie tuxedo, the insulated jacket has become a cold-weather closet staple.A 1920s version by Australian mountaineer Geo
deduped_items.body_text:
Whether you call it a parka, puffer or Tassie tuxedo, the insulated jacket has become a cold-weather closet staple.
A 1920s version by Australian mountaineer George Finch was constructed from hot air balloon fabric and eiderdown, but most modern designs are a mix of petroleum-based synthetics as well as animal and plant fibres, with varying environmental and ethical impacts.
Producing these materials, through agricultural or chemical processes, contributes 83% to the jacket’s overall carbon and water footprint, according to one life cycle study. The next largest contributor was water and energy usage during wear – with the average down jacket lasting seven years – followed by sewing and disposal. Natural fibres like down and wool also add animal welfare considerations.
But, like all clothing items, the effects are multiplied across global production and consumption systems. The market for puffers is large and growing, with more than 100m jackets made in China annually. Some brands are even branching into new territory, with demand for puppy puffers soaring.
Dr Carolina Quintero Rodriguez, a senior lecturer at RMIT University’s school of fashion and textiles, says advertising and social media are encouraging us to purchase more than we need.
“That is incentivising or creating a need in the population for not only one jacket, but you need three jackets,” she says.
A recent Adelaide University study of nearly 600 people’s clothing habits found 89% of garments are bought new, with padded jackets one of the most expensive items that people own, but rarely wear, which provides a ready supply of secondhand puffers in great condition. That’s why it’s important to choose a good quality garment, from a responsible brand, and wear it and repair it for as long as possible.
One jacket, many ingredients
Julie Boulton, a sustainable fashion consultant, says puffers usually consist of an inner and outer shell, a filler (“the stuff that makes it puff”), and notions like zips, snaps or buttons and thread.
Shells are usually made from fossil fuel-derived materials, such as nylon or polyester, sometimes blended with cotton or wool.
Jackets labelled “100% recycled” usually comprise polyesters made from plastic waste, such as water bottles or used textiles.
The padding inside often consists of duck or goose feathers (called down), wool, or a synthetic fill, Boulton says. Some brands, like Pangaia, are moving to plant-based fluff, made from wildflowers, biopolymers and aerogel.
According to the life cycle study, polyester fibre production, spinning, weaving, fabric dyeing and finishing are all high-energy consumption processes.
Polyester is a petroleum-based fibre that has issues with greenhouse gas emissions and shedding microplastics, Quintero Rodriguez says. Natural down is biodegradable and a byproduct of the meat industry, she says, but can come with risks associated with animal welfare and supply chain opacity.
Down is made by plucking the soft feathers of ducks or geese, usually after slaughter, according to the RSPCA, although a small percentage (1 to 2%) is still thought to be collected from live plucking, a practice the organisation says is a major welfare concern. Consumers are encouraged to look for the Responsible Down Standard, a voluntary certification that requires higher levels of animal welfare, traceability and prohibits live plucking.
When it comes to wool, Dr Natalie Roadknight, a senior scientific officer at the RSPCA, says the biggest welfare concern is a practice called mulesing, which involves cutting an area of skin near the tail. “It’s done while the lamb is completely conscious,” she says. “They’re able to feel the cuts”. Australia is one of the only countries where the practice is still legal, with the procedure banned in New Zealand and other countries.
Consumers can choose to avoid wool products that involve mulesing, by asking the brand directly, or looking for the ZQ Merino or the Responsible Wool Standard.

deduped_items.title: Editorial: Temoac: explicaciones urgentes
deduped_items.summary: El secretario de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana, Omar García Harfuch, confirmó ayer que Valentín Lavín Romero, alcalde de Temoac asesinado el pasado miércoles, estuvo involucrado en los asesinatos de los activistas Samir Flores y Sandra Rosa Camacho. El funcionario informó que esa línea de investigación la lleva la Fiscalía del estado de Morelos (FGJ), pero que también se le seguía por sus posibles nexos con células delictivas como Los Aparicio y Los Huazulco, vinculadas a delitos de alto impa
deduped_items.body_text:
l secretario de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana, Omar García Harfuch, confirmó ayer que Valentín Lavín Romero, alcalde de Temoac asesinado el pasado miércoles, estuvo involucrado en los asesinatos de los activistas Samir Flores y Sandra Rosa Camacho. El funcionario informó que esa línea de investigación la lleva la Fiscalía del estado de Morelos (FGJ), pero que también se le seguía por sus posibles nexos con células delictivas como Los Aparicio y Los Huazulco, vinculadas a delitos de alto impacto como secuestro, extorsión, cobro de piso y narcomenudeo en la zona oriente de la entidad. Asimismo, recordó que Lavín Romero sufrió una agresión en enero de este año, “lo que originó trabajos de investigación por parte de las autoridades”, e incluso ya se había detenido a varios de sus familiares, incluidos sus suegros.
El político que gobernaba bajo las siglas del Partido Verde Ecologista de México (PVEM) ya había encabezado el ayuntamiento en el periodo 2019-2021, cuando fue asesinado Samir Flores Soberanes, integrante del Frente de Pueblos en Defensa de la Tierra y el Agua de Morelos, Puebla y Tlaxcala (FPDT). Ante la muerte de Lavín, la organización recordó que “desde el inicio fue considerado como uno de los probables responsables del homicidio, pero nunca fue llamado a declarar”. Asimismo, los miembros del FPDT reclaman que el presidente municipal no haya sido arrestado en el marco del Operativo Enjambre, pese a que desde hace años han denunciado “su relación directa con la célula del crimen organizado Los Aparicio, comandada por su suegra, Angelina N, quien fue tesorera del gobierno de Temoac durante la administración 2021-2023 y fue detenida el año pasado acusada de extorsión, secuestro, narcotráfico, homicidio y delincuencia organizada”.
Las autoridades deben explicar de manera creíble la exasperante lentitud en las indagatorias en torno a Lavín, así como el hecho de que nunca se le haya citado a declarar por el crimen contra Flores Soberanes, del que se cumplieron siete años en febrero pasado. Es inadmisible, por ejemplo, que no se haya integrado un expediente que permitiera, al menos, hacerlo comparecer tras la detención de su suegra y que se hayan ignorado de manera sistemática los señalamientos de sus nexos delictivos. Además de las falencias en las instancias de procuración de justicia, pesa una responsabilidad sobre los organismos electorales y las fuerzas políticas que le facilitaron el acceso al poder sin verificar sus antecedentes o, peor, estando al tanto de ellos.
Por último, si las acusaciones hacia Lavín Romero resultan ciertas, es deplorable que se haya permitido su impunidad por tanto tiempo y que con su muerte se haya echado otra capa de silencio en torno a los autores materiales del asesinato de Samir Flores, uno de los casos más emblemáticos por los que la sociedad morelense sigue exigiendo justicia.
Cabe esperar que las autoridades estatales y federales se consagren a subsanar los errores, esclarecer los delitos en los que pudo estar implicado el fallecido edil y devolver la paz al oriente de Morelos, una de las zonas del país más azotadas por la inseguridad.

deduped_items.body_text:
l secretario de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana, Omar García Harfuch, confirmó ayer que Valentín Lavín Romero, alcalde de Temoac asesinado el pasado miércoles, estuvo involucrado en los asesinatos de los activistas Samir Flores y Sandra Rosa Camacho. El funcionario informó que esa línea de investigación la lleva la Fiscalía del estado de Morelos (FGJ), pero que también se le seguía por sus posibles nexos con células delictivas como Los Aparicio y Los Huazulco, vinculadas a delitos de alto impacto como secuestro, extorsión, cobro de piso y narcomenudeo en la zona oriente de la entidad. Asimismo, recordó que Lavín Romero sufrió una agresión en enero de este año, “lo que originó trabajos de investigación por parte de las autoridades”, e incluso ya se había detenido a varios de sus familiares, incluidos sus suegros.
El político que gobernaba bajo las siglas del Partido Verde Ecologista de México (PVEM) ya había encabezado el ayuntamiento en el periodo 2019-2021, cuando fue asesinado Samir Flores Soberanes, integrante del Frente de Pueblos en Defensa de la Tierra y el Agua de Morelos, Puebla y Tlaxcala (FPDT). Ante la muerte de Lavín, la organización recordó que “desde el inicio fue considerado como uno de los probables responsables del homicidio, pero nunca fue llamado a declarar”. Asimismo, los miembros del FPDT reclaman que el presidente municipal no haya sido arrestado en el marco del Operativo Enjambre, pese a que desde hace años han denunciado “su relación directa con la célula del crimen organizado Los Aparicio, comandada por su suegra, Angelina N, quien fue tesorera del gobierno de Temoac durante la administración 2021-2023 y fue detenida el año pasado acusada de extorsión, secuestro, narcotráfico, homicidio y delincuencia organizada”.
Las autoridades deben explicar de manera creíble la exasperante lentitud en las indagatorias en torno a Lavín, así como el hecho de que nunca se le haya citado a declarar por el crimen contra Flores Soberanes, del que se cumplieron siete años en febrero pasado. Es inadmisible, por ejemplo, que no se haya integrado un expediente que permitiera, al menos, hacerlo comparecer tras la detención de su suegra y que se hayan ignorado de manera sistemática los señalamientos de sus nexos delictivos. Además de las falencias en las instancias de procuración de justicia, pesa una responsabilidad sobre los organismos electorales y las fuerzas políticas que le facilitaron el acceso al poder sin verificar sus antecedentes o, peor, estando al tanto de ellos.
Por último, si las acusaciones hacia Lavín Romero resultan ciertas, es deplorable que se haya permitido su impunidad por tanto tiempo y que con su muerte se haya echado otra capa de silencio en torno a los autores materiales del asesinato de Samir Flores, uno de los casos más emblemáticos por los que la sociedad morelense sigue exigiendo justicia.
Cabe esperar que las autoridades estatales y federales se consagren a subsanar los errores, esclarecer los delitos en los que pudo estar implicado el fallecido edil y devolver la paz al oriente de Morelos, una de las zonas del país más azotadas por la inseguridad.

deduped_items.title: Y un día, la derrota se festejó como un triunfo
deduped_items.summary: Se llegó alto. Pero la ambición era llegar a lo más alto. De allí la frustración que sobrevino a la derrota. La selección argentina enfrentó un equipo que jugó mucho mejor y nos cortó el ascenso a la gloria, cuando estaba tan cerca que ya la dábamos por nuestra. Es un grupo maravilloso y merecía la gloria. Pero no mereció ganar el partido. Se perdió con justicia. Hubo corazón. Faltó fútbol.Hubo corazón para defender, no para atacar. No hubo hambre de gol y no se buscó el arco. Los nuestros, incl

deduped_items.title: Hantavirus in Venezuela: What It Means, and What It Doesn’t
deduped_items.summary: Recent cases of hantavirus infection in Venezuela are not a cause for panic. They do, however, underscore the country's urgent need for transparent, timely, and readily accessible epidemiological data
deduped_items.body_text:
Hantavirus in Venezuela: What It Means, and What It Doesn't
Recent cases of hantavirus infection in Venezuela are not a cause for panic. They do, however, underscore the country's urgent need for transparent, timely, and readily accessible epidemiological data
The truth isn’t out there but at the Rafael Rangel National Hygiene Institute (INH)
Earlier this week, Venezuela’s Ministry of Health announced the deaths of three people in a small town in eastern Venezuela from hantavirus infection. The news quickly spread across social media and reached international headlines, partly because many associated it with the recent outbreak aboard the MV Hondius, a cruise ship sailing in the South Atlantic, where eleven passengers were infected and three died last May.
The two events, however, are unrelated.
Hantaviruses are a diverse family of viruses that naturally infect a wide variety of rodents and only occasionally spill over into humans. Infection usually occurs after exposure to contaminated rodent urine or feces, most commonly through inhaling virus-containing particles suspended in dust. Less frequently, transmission can occur through contaminated food, or through contact with blood, saliva, or bites from infected animals.
Human-to-human transmission has been documented only for the Andes virus, which circulates in southern Chile and Argentina and was responsible for the outbreak aboard the Hondius. Although Venezuelan authorities have not yet identified the virus responsible for the recent deaths, there is no reason to believe it is the Andes virus, which has never been detected in the country.
Instead, Venezuela is home to at least two native hantaviruses: Caño Delgadito and Maporal, named after the locations in Portuguesa and Barinas states where they were first identified. Unlike the Andes virus, neither has been shown to spread from person to person. As a result, the likelihood of community transmission or a nationwide outbreak is extremely low.
Because the rodents that carry these viruses are most common in rural environments, infections primarily affect agricultural workers and people who are regularly exposed to contaminated soil, grain storage facilities, or forestgoers.
Although this may be the first time many Venezuelans hear about hantavirus in the country, the disease is not new. Sporadic outbreaks have been reported since the first confirmed human case was identified in 1993. Besides the current cluster in Boca del Pao, Anzoátegui state, cases were last reported in Delta Amacuro in 2024 and in Portuguesa last year.
Detailed epidemiological information about these outbreaks has remained scarce, reflecting the longstanding lack of transparency surrounding official public health data in Venezuela.
Similarly, little is known about the three recent deaths in Anzoátegui beyond the fact that all three victims belonged to the same family.
Despite its apparent rarity, hantavirus infection in Venezuela is probably more common than reported. The rodent species that carry these viruses are widely distributed across Portuguesa, Barinas, Guárico, Cojedes, Anzoátegui, Delta Amacuro, and Bolívar states. Moreover, a 2013 serological study detected antibodies against hantaviruses in nearly 2% of more than 1,300 blood samples collected throughout the country.
These findings suggest that human exposure to hantaviruses is geographically widespread, even if infection and severe disease remain uncommon.
One reason the disease receives relatively little attention is that it can easily be mistaken for other febrile illnesses common in Venezuela, particularly dengue. Diagnosing hantavirus infection requires a high degree of clinical suspicion together with specialized laboratory testing, which is only available at the Rafael Rangel National Hygiene Institute (INH) and the Centre for Research on Hemorrhagic Viral Infections and Transmissible Diseases (CIVIHET) in Guanare, Portuguesa.

deduped_items.title: OPEN SECRETS: Digital Profiteers (Part One): A peek behind South Africa’s digitalised grants system
deduped_items.summary: In the past year, Open Secrets investigated the role of commercial banks in the administration of the Social Relief of Distress grant. Documents we have obtained reveal the banks are contracted by the Department of Social Development and the South African Social Security Agency to digitally verify grant beneficiaries’ income status and dispense grant payments from Sassa. In three articles we unpack the questions the investigation raised about accountability and transparency as the government rel
deduped_items.body_text:
Living near the coastal edges of Amanzimtoti, KwaZulu-Natal, Buhle Sibya was unemployed and viewed the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant as a chance to take care of herself and her daughter. In March 2021 she successfully applied for the grant, then only R350. It was paid to her every month until January 2023 when she was notified that her approval for the grant had been declined.
In her testimony to the Pretoria High Court, she explained the reason for the decline: It âwas said to be that the bank verification process had determined I had additional income. This was not true. The only income I had received was the amount of R1,000 towards the burial of my late motherâ¦ who had, at the time, just died. Because of the loss of support of the grant, I can no longer support my daughter or my own self.â
Her testimony was one of 79 brought forward to the high court in 2023 documenting the inadequacies of amended regulations related to the SRD grant introduced in 2023. The case was brought against the Department of Social Development (DSD) and the South African Social Security Agency (Sassa) by civil society organisations the Institute of Economic Justice and #PayTheGrants, with National Treasury joining later to oppose the case.
An important issue in the case was the flaws in the digital income verification using banks to assess SRD grant beneficiariesâ income status. The DSD insisted: âThe bank verification system is one of the most effective and accurate mechanisms used to retrieve the SRD applicantâs financial means for the particular month concerned.â
However, on 23 January 2025, Judge Leonard Twala declared the use of income verification through the banks in SRD applications unconstitutional.
The judgment deemed verification through the banks to be exclusionary and ordered the government to improve it. Additionally, it ordered the R370 payment be raised to R624 and that it is unlawful for SRD grant applications to only be conducted online.
On 13 February 2025, the DSD, Sassa and National Treasury appealed the judgment, arguing the entire ruling is flawed. The case hearing is set for 25 August 2026 in the Supreme Court of Appeal. As a consequence, Twalaâs court ruling is suspended until the appeal is heard. In that time, government can continue to expand its digitised processes in grants administration.
Documents obtained by Open Secrets reveal that Sassa contracted Absa Bank, African Bank, FNB, Nedbank, Standard Bank and Tyme Bank to conduct means tests on SRD grant applicants and beneficiaries, as well as for other social grants, between 1 March 2025 and 31 July 2027.
They provide detailed information on how this process with the banks works. In this article, we explain why the South African government relies on banks in the income verification process for social grants, and how addressing current failures requires more inclusion of what grant recipients need from the new digital system.
The SRD grant and inaccurate public databases
Six years ago, the Covid-19 pandemic decimated the livelihoods of millions of people across South Africa, leaving many with no source of income. In March 2021 she successfully applied for the grant, then only R350. It was paid to her every month until January 2023 when she was notified that her approval for the grant had been declined.
In her testimony to the Pretoria High Court, she explained the reason for the decline: It âwas said to be that the bank verification process had determined I had additional income. This was not true. The only income I had received was the amount of R1,000 towards the burial of my late motherâ¦ who had, at the time, just died. Because of the loss of support of the grant, I can no longer support my daughter or my own self.â
Her testimony was one of 79 brought forward to the high court in 2023 documenting the inadequacies of amended regulations related to the SRD grant introduced in 2023. The case was brought against the Department of Social Development (DSD) and the South African Social Security Agency (Sassa) by civil society organisations the Institute of Economic Justice and #PayTheGrants, with National Treasury joining later to oppose the case.
An important issue in the case was the flaws in the digital income verification using banks to assess SRD grant beneficiariesâ income status. The DSD insisted: âThe bank verification system is one of the most effective and accurate mechanisms used to retrieve the SRD applicantâs financial means for the particular month concerned.â
However, on 23 January 2025, Judge Leonard Twala declared the use of income verification through the banks in SRD applications unconstitutional.
The judgment deemed verification through the banks to be exclusionary and ordered the government to improve it. Additionally, it ordered the R370 payment be raised to R624 and that it is unlawful for SRD grant applications to only be conducted online.
On 13 February 2025, the DSD, Sassa and National Treasury appealed the judgment, arguing the entire ruling is flawed. The case hearing is set for 25 August 2026 in the Supreme Court of Appeal. As a consequence, Twalaâs court ruling is suspended until the appeal is heard. In that time, government can continue to expand its digitised processes in grants administration.
Documents obtained by Open Secrets reveal that Sassa contracted Absa Bank, African Bank, FNB, Nedbank, Standard Bank and Tyme Bank to conduct means tests on SRD grant applicants and beneficiaries, as well as for other social grants, between 1 March 2025 and 31 July 2027.
They provide detailed information on how this process with the banks works. In this article, we explain why the South African government relies on banks in the income verification process for social grants, and how addressing current failures requires more inclusion of what grant recipients need from the new digital system.
The SRD grant and inaccurate public databases
Six years ago, the Covid-19 pandemic decimated the livelihoods of millions of people across South Africa, leaving many with no source of income. In response, the government introduced the special R350 Covid-19 SRD grant. Due to the nature of the pandemic, the SRD grant became the first grant where applications took place completely online.
In late September 2025, Sassa executive manager of grants operations Brenton van Vrede sat down with Open Secrets investigators for an on-the-record interview. Reflecting on the Covid crisis, Van Vrede noted that the agency needed an immediate approach to deliver a new grant:
âThe Covid SRD grantâ¦required a very rapid, quick responseâ¦ Itâs about how do you reach as many people in a lockdown situation as fast as possible without any human contact due to the nature of Covid.â
The answer: digitalise the SRD grant and administer it fully online. But Sassa faced a problem. An effective digitalised administration of a new social grant requires efficient technolog

deduped_items.title: Ethiopia: U.S.-Ethiopia Public Private Dialogue to Benefit U.S. and Ethiopian Businesses and Economic Growth
deduped_items.summary: [U.S. Embassy Addis Ababa] Addis Ababa -- U.S. Ambassador to Ethiopia Ervin J. Massinga co-chaired a Public-Private Dialogue (PPD) with Ethiopian Investment Commission (EIC) Commissioner Dr. Zeleke Temesgen and Chief Macroeconomic Advisor to the Prime Minister Ambassador Girma Biru at the Skylight Hotel in Addis Ababa on July 23. The dialogue focused on advancing commercial diplomacy, expanding market access, and ensuring a level playing field for U.S. companies operating in Ethiopia. By bringin

Massinga co-chaired a Public-Private Dialogue (PPD) with Ethiopian Investment Commission (EIC) Commissioner Dr. Zeleke Temesgen and Chief Macroeconomic Advisor to the Prime Minister Ambassador Girma Biru at the Skylight Hotel in Addis Ababa on July 23. The dialogue focused on advancing commercial diplomacy, expanding market access, and ensuring a level playing field for U.S. companies operating in Ethiopia. By bringin

deduped_items.title: Sénégal: le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye doit dévoiler le nom de son nouveau parti
deduped_items.summary: Nouvelle étape ce samedi 25 juillet 2026 pour les partisans de Bassirou Diomaye Faye. La coalition « Diomaye Président » doit officiellement laisser la place à un nouveau parti, annoncé le vendredi 3 juillet 2026, dont le nom sera dévoilé lors d’une Assemblée générale constitutive. Le chef de l’État devrait en prendre la présidence. Cette naissance intervient dans un contexte de départs remarqués, tant au sein des Patriotes africains du Sénégal pour le travail, l'éthique et la fraternité (Pastef
deduped_items.normalised_title: sénégal le président bassirou diomaye faye doit dévoiler le nom de son nouveau parti

deduped_items.title: Tunisie: cinq ans après le coup constitutionnel de Kaïs Saïed, la colère monte
deduped_items.summary: En Tunisie, le 25 juillet marque l’anniversaire de la proclamation de la République tunisienne en 1957. Mais cette date est aujourd’hui aussi celle des cinq ans du coup constitutionnel du président Kaïs Saïed. Le 25 juillet 2021, sur fond de crise sanitaire et politique, le président du pays depuis 2019 s’empare des pouvoirs, limoge le gouvernement et gèle les travaux du Parlement, décrétant un état d’exception. Cinq ans plus tard, le pays vit une dérive autoritaire et une période de fortes tens
deduped_items.normalised_title: tunisie cinq ans après le coup constitutionnel de kaïs saïed la colère monte

deduped_items.title: Why is Cair urging US Muslims to seek security from DHS?
deduped_items.summary: Why is Cair urging US Muslims to seek security from DHS? Submitted by Muneeza Rizvi on Fri, 06/26/2026 - 22:15 The grant push is only the latest in the civil rights group's decades of steering Muslims towards the institutions that surveil, entrap and deport them Police and officials brief the media after a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego on 18 May 2026 (Carlos A Moreno/Getty Images via AFP) Off Applications for this year's round of security grants from the US Department of Homeland S
deduped_items.body_text:
Why is Cair urging US Muslims to seek security from DHS?
Applications for this year's round of security grants from the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) close on 24 July - and the Council on American-Islamic Relations (Cair) is urging mosques, Islamic schools and Muslim nonprofits to apply before the deadline.
Since May's mosque shooting in San Diego, which killed three people, Cair has aggressively pursued renewed Muslim community access to this source of government funding, presenting it as a means of protecting mosques from such violence.
Cair has since also encouraged Muslims to build closer ties with the police - reviving a debate over policing that reflects a growing divide within the community, between those eager to collaborate with "law enforcement" and those who view it as an arm of an unjust social order.
Cair has long walked an ambivalent line on this issue. As a self-described civil rights and advocacy nonprofit with nearly 30 chapters, it positions itself as Muslims' primary defence against "overly-broad" policing.
Yet, at the same time, it has spent decades encouraging Muslims to "build bridges" with the very police agencies whose practices it claims to challenge.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Cair's encouragement suggests that Muslims and "law enforcement" are two groups separated by unfamiliarity or misunderstanding. However, the history between them is not one of insufficient contact.
Muslims have come to know local and federal police agencies all too well through a history of hostile encounters: decades of FBI door knocks, entrapment cases, raids of Palestine encampments that local police have turned into prosecutions of Muslim students, harassment outside Zionist land sales and relentless attempts to conscript Muslims into disciplining their own communities.
Though spread unevenly, suspicion towards "law enforcement" has long existed among Muslims in the United States. Such sentiments became more visible in 2020, during the nationwide demonstrations following the police murder of George Floyd. And they have only become more pronounced since Israel's genocidal war in Palestine.
Indeed, when any meaningful resistance to US foreign policy is met with police violence, it becomes difficult to ignore the link between occupation abroad and state repression at home. Despite this growing political consciousness among Muslims, Cair remains committed to strengthening Muslim cooperation with "law enforcement".
'Best practices'
In the aftermath of the shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, numerous Cair branches disseminated the national office's "Best Practices for Mosque and Community Safety", a booklet aimed at leaders and everyday congregants. Its recommendations take as given that Muslims embracing "law enforcement" will protect mosques from violence and desecration.
Best practices listed in the document thus include informing local police of mosques' daily schedules, inviting police to mosques for meetings and offering police training in cultural competency.
Recommendations also extend beyond local "law enforcement". The booklet stresses: "Attempt to establish liaison with state and federal agencies in the same manner as you did with the local police. Local police may be able to facilitate this effort."
Cair's best practices appear less concerned with Muslim defence than with having Muslims project respectability
It also reminds congregations unable to afford private inspections of their security protocols that police departments can offer such assessments, as can specialists from DHS.
Most bizarre is the booklet's jumble of non-evidence-based suggestions for deterring anti-Muslim violence. For example, it urges mosques to "acknowledge good work by individual police officers" and other local officials through "complimentary letters, phone calls, tweets, social media postin

deduped_items.body_text:
Israeli forces conduct widespread raids across Jenin
Israeli forces conducted large-scale raids in Jenin and surrounding towns on Saturday morning, Wafa news agency is reporting, citing local sources.
According to the sources, Israeli troops stormed the city's neighbourhoods of Jabal Abu Dhahir and Al-Marah as well as the towns and villages of Zababdeh, Faqqu'a, Ya'bad, Burqin, Jalbun, Qabatiya, Jalqamus, Silat al-Harithiya, Ya'mun, Kafr Dan, Deir Abu Da'if and Zububa.
Wafa reported that forces also raided housing where residents displaced from Jenin refugee camp had been sheltering.
Earlier, Al Jazeera reported that two Palestinians had been wounded in a fresh wave of Israeli military raids and settler attacks across the occupied West Bank overnight.
Israeli troops raided some 70 homes and detained around 50 Palestinians in the town of Tal, southwest of Nablus.

deduped_items.title: JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings
deduped_items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China’s JD.com has partnered with Iraqi digital commerce platform GINI to increase access to its goods in Iraq, marking the latest step toward developing the country’s rapidly […] The post JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings appeared first on Iraqi News.
deduped_items.body_text:
JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China’s JD.com has partnered with Iraqi digital commerce platform GINI to increase access to its goods in Iraq, marking the latest step toward developing the country’s rapidly expanding e-commerce industry.
The deal would integrate JD.com’s product catalog into GINI’s digital marketplace and the SuperQi app, providing Iraqi customers with greater access to items from one of China’s top online retailers.
The agreement aims to establish a direct supply chain between JD.com and the Iraqi market, thereby enhancing product availability and facilitating cross-border online buying.
GINI, an Iraqi digital commerce and market automation platform, combines merchants, delivery providers, and payment services in a unified ecosystem, allowing companies to manage sales, payments, and logistics.
JD.com, founded in 1998, is China’s largest retailer by revenue and one of the country’s leading e-commerce companies, with a vast logistics network that enables rapid order fulfillment across China and international markets.
The agreement comes as Iraq’s e-commerce sector grows, along with rising internet penetration, digital payment adoption, and government efforts to modernize the economy and encourage more private sector investment in technology and digital services.
Baghdad has increasingly pushed to recruit multinational technology businesses and digital commerce platforms as part of larger attempts to diversify the economy away from oil, generate private-sector employment, and enhance access to products and services via online markets.

deduped_items.summary: شن الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترامب هجوما على ما وصفها بـ"وسائل الإعلام الكاذبة"، وتحدّث مازحا عن احتمال تولّيه ولاية رئاسية ثالثة، وذلك خلال مشاركته في عشاء رابطة مراسلي البيت الأبيض الذي أُعيد تنظيمه الجمعة، وسط إجراءات أمنية مشدّدة، بعد ثلاثة أشهر من حادثة إطلاق نار أجبرته على مغادرة الحفلة. وتضمن برنامج الأمسية الجديدة فقرات مشابهة للاحتفال الأصلي، بينها عرض للفنان الذهني أوز بيرلمان، وتكريم لأحد عناصر الخدمة السرية، الذي ساعد في إيقاف المشتبه به خلال إطلاق النار في نيسان/أبريل الماضي.

deduped_items.title: Venezuela: refugiados se niegan a ser reubicados hasta que no aparezcan sus familiares
deduped_items.summary: Este 24 de junio se cumple un mes del doble terremoto que sacudió a Venezuela y que, según las autoridades, dejó más de 5.300 muertos; no obstante, grupos ciudadanos y ONG afirman que hay miles de personas aún debajo de los escombros y cuya vida ya se da por perdida. Cientos de personas se encuentran refugiadas en condiciones precarias en carpas, donde llegan aseguran llegan descansar después de pasar horas frente a los edificios destruidos donde esperan encontrar a sus familiares. deduped_items.title: South African court rules on Ramaphosa impeachment hearings
deduped_items.summary: A South African court has temporarily halted public impeachment hearings against President Cyril Ramaphosa over alleged financial misconduct Read Full Article at RT.com
deduped_items.body_text:
South African court rules on Ramaphosa impeachment hearings
A South African court has temporarily halted public impeachment hearings against President Cyril Ramaphosa over a long-running scandal involving $580,000 stolen from his private game farm.
The Western Cape High Court ruled on Friday that Parliament’s Section 89 impeachment committee could not proceed with public hearings until it decides Ramaphosa’s separate application to overturn the report underpinning the inquiry.
The 2-1 majority ruling does not prevent the committee from continuing preparatory work. Its chairman, Makashule Gana, said members would study the judgment to determine “which aspect of the work we can proceed with.”
Ramaphosa’s office welcomed the decision, saying the president “reaffirms his respect of judicial independence and separation of powers” and would continue to cooperate with accountability processes.
The case stems from the Phala Phala scandal, a 2020 burglary at Ramaphosa’s private game farm in Limpopo, where Ramaphosa claims that around $580,000 in foreign currency hidden in a couch was stolen. However, former spy boss Arthur Fraser alleged that the sum was in fact $4 million. Ramaphosa has denied any wrongdoing, saying the money came from a legitimate sale of buffaloes.
An independent parliamentary panel concluded in 2022 that there was prima facie evidence that Ramaphosa may have violated the law and his oath of office. The National Assembly rejected the report that year, when the African National Congress (ANC) held a parliamentary majority.
However, the Constitutional Court overturned that decision in May, ruling that Parliament acted irrationally, and ordered the report to be referred to an impeachment committee for review. Ramaphosa subsequently asked the High Court to set the report aside, arguing that it relied on hearsay and failed to distinguish prima facie from sufficient evidence. That challenge is expected to be heard in September.
Opposition parties have criticized the ruling, with African Transformation Movement leader Vuyo Zungula describing it as “nothing else but a delay,” South African broadcaster eNCA reported. The uMkhonto weSizwe Party also expressed disappointment, while Democratic Alliance MP Glynnis Breytenbach said the outcome “was to be expected” and would not prevent the impeachment committee from continuing its preparatory work.
If the committee ultimately finds grounds for impeachment, Ramaphosa’s removal would require support from at least two-thirds (267) of the 400-member National Assembly. His ANC lost its majority in 2024 but still holds 159 seats, enough to block impeachment if its lawmakers remain united. The party now governs through a ten-party Government of National Unity that includes the Democratic Alliance, the second-largest party, and several smaller parties.

deduped_items.title: British Army faces Kenya setback amid row over troops’ crimes
deduped_items.summary: The British Ministry of Defence has said it was forced to cancel a major army exercise in Kenya after failing to obtain the required license Read Full Article at RT.com
deduped_items.body_text:
British Army faces Kenya setback amid row over troops’ crimes
The UK has canceled a major army exercise in Kenya after the two countries failed to resolve a dispute over Nairobi’s powers to prosecute British soldiers accused of committing crimes in the East African nation.
The planned Exercise Haraka Storm, involving the 1st Battalion and The Duke of Lancaster’s Regiment, was reportedly scheduled to begin in September in central Kenya’s Laikipia County. It will instead be held outside Kenya, the British Ministry of Defence said on Thursday, according to The Guardian. Kenya’s Standard newspaper reported that the training would be moved to neighboring Tanzania. 
“It is with regret that the necessary licences required to allow training to take place in Laikipia later this year have not been forthcoming,” a Ministry of Defence spokesperson said.
The African state hosts a permanent British Army training support unit, known as BATUK, in Nanyuki, about 200km (125 miles) north of the capital, Nairobi. British troops have trained there since Kenya’s independence in 1963, conducting infantry exercises, as well as engineering and medical deployments under a bilateral defense cooperation agreement.
Kenyan lawmakers have, however, withheld approval for a renewed bilateral defense agreement amid demands for greater jurisdiction over serious offenses committed by British troops. Funding for BATUK is also reportedly under negotiation.
The unit has faced widespread allegations of misconduct, including murder, rape, and environmental pollution. A two-year Kenyan parliamentary investigation report released last December accused British soldiers of murder, sexual assault, torture, and forcibly evicting residents near Nanyuki. It also documented claims involving civilian deaths and injuries from unexploded ordnance, pollution, toxic-waste disposal, and damage to wildlife habitats.
Former serviceman Robert Purkiss has been charged in Kenya with the 2012 murder of 21-year-old Agnes Wanjiru. He is contesting extradition from Britain. Wanjiru’s body was found in a septic tank near a Nanyuki hotel after she was last seen with British troops. Purkiss denies the charge.
Last year, Britain agreed to pay £2.9 million ($3.9 million) to more than 7,700 Kenyans and an environmental group over a 2021 wildfire accidentally started by British troops. The blaze destroyed more than 12,000 acres of the Lolldaiga Hills and reportedly caused one death.
The Ministry of Defence said it remained committed to its defense partnership with Kenya and would continue talks aimed at resuming training.
Nelson Koech, chairman of the Kenyan parliament’s defense committee, said Nairobi is seeking stronger accountability measures, greater protection for local communities, and implementation of the BATUK inquiry’s recommendations.
The two governments are “actively engaging to address these outstanding issues,” The Guardian quoted Koech as saying.

deduped_items.summary: At the end of his six-day mission to Ukraine, Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher reflects on the resilience of a people "willing to suffer for freedom and peace." Speaking to Vatican Media, the Holy See's Secretary for Relations with States recalls those who have "lost everything," reiterates the Holy See's commitment to humanitarian efforts and peace, and says Pope Leo XIV takes seriously the invitation to visit Ukraine when the time and circumstances can be "as fruitful as possible." deduped_items.summary: ROME (AP) — The Vatican has long considered any sexual relations between a priest and an adult as sinful but consensual, and only criminalizes the behavior if the adult “habitually lacks the use of reason.”
